scope: Three adaptive MediaMTX 1.21.1 trials on one independent Linux x64 runner with identical producer, browser and distributor image digests. Public 3s down-hold; 720p30 / 540p24 / 360p15 ladder; 1500 kbit/s producer-to-adapter capacity; no injected loss/delay; zero playout-delay hint.

All three trials pass all 23 gates, including visible startup, decoded formats/cadence, source-target recovery, required native boundaries and teardown. Baseline, steady capacity and recovery native frozen time are zero. Initial capacity-transition freezes are 1.721s, 1.912s and 1.664s, within the unchanged three-second budget.
First observed visible frames arrive 625.9ms, 891.1ms and 868.7ms after Connect. These finite synthetic-source observations exclude process boot, physical capture/display and target hardware.

The qualification-only signaling proxies use unpublished Docker ports and adapter loopback; producer and adapter media remain in separate network namespaces. No rstream tunnel, TURN, edge authentication, Next.js or GitHub OAuth is exercised. Their separate authenticated qualification records remain required.

This independent success does not reclassify historical local failures or establish the cause of local 207ms/231ms baseline freezes. It qualifies this revision and runner environment; production timings and continuity thresholds are unchanged.
